external_entities.name: customers
external_entities.description: People who browse and order socks through the mobile app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the customers' trust zone.

external_entities.name: marketing
external_entities.description: The marketing staff who maintain the catalogue spreadsheet.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the marketing staff's trust zone.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application customers use to browse and order socks.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API that serves the mobile app, keeps customer records, and hands orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: stock and inventory system
processes.description: SIMS, the stock and inventory system that receives orders from the web API and sends dispatch information onward.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS, our stock and inventory system
processes.notes: The text says SIMS has been running since long before the app existed.

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that sends dispatch notes by fax to customers.
processes.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway
processes.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order, and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the catalogue spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and the cards they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing delivery addresses only.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted. Being kept alongside SIMS does not establish a trust-zone placement.

data_stores.name: catalogue spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The marketing catalogue spreadsheet containing prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

data_flows.name: mobile app requests
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keep customer records
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and the card they paid with

data_flows.name: hand over order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: write delivery address
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file

data_flows.name: send dispatch note
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: fax confirmation
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

data_flows.name: change catalogue
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop holding the catalogue spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is internet-facing because customers use the mobile app to browse and order online through it.
assumptions.basis: The description says Sokify sells socks online, customers use the mobile app to browse and order, and the app talks to the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface because the text identifies it as a mobile app and explicitly says there is no website.
assumptions.basis: The description says customers use the mobile app and that there is no website.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment-card information.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are personal and payment data.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains customers' delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The stated contents are delivery addresses, which are personal data.
